utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, let me first introduce to you, or give my apologies from Geoffrey Nice who will not be able to be with us this afternoon because he is working in the Jelisic case, and that is that case is meeting at the same time as this one, the Kordic case. I would also like to say that at the request of the witness who will appear this afternoon, that we have filed a motion that the witness be granted protective measures. So that I can present it to you, I would like us to be able to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, after the 1990 elections and until June of 1992, would you say that the working relations within the municipal institutions in Novi Travnik between the Croats and Muslims were good until June 1992, the time when the HVO attacked certain institutions within the city of Novi Travnik? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one could say that relations were more or less good sometime up until April '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: April 1992. That corresponds with the establishment of the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly, yes. In April 1992, the first flag of Herceg-Bosna was hoisted, the flag of the Croatian people, a flag with Croatian emblems, on the municipality. This was on the 10th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that period in April 1992, were there some events that took place in the municipality of Novi Travnik which dealt with the sending of weapons and ammunition from the Bratstvo factory to the JNA, and the Croats in the region were opposed to that type of delivery? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was so. Since in Novi Travnik, there was the military factory, Bratstvo, which mostly manufactured all kinds of weapons, including heavy weapons, and as there was a conflict going on in Croatia at the same time against the JNA, they opposed deliveries of weapons from Bratstvo to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that certain trucks that were carrying those weapons and ammunition were stopped and that the Croats seized some of the trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I know of one truck which was stopped in the village of Bucici, but I don't know what happened with that truck or the weapons and equipment. What happened with it, I don't know. I know that it was stopped at the village of Bucici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croats that we are speaking about had seized the trucks by force; is that correct? The trucks that we are speaking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The truck was stopped by armed civilians, and some, by then, soldiers with weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, notice at that time that there were armed civilians and soldiers preventing the traffic of those vehicles in the area of Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was in that period that traffic was stopped in that area; that is, the area from Bucici towards the crossroads on the Travnik/Sarajevo highway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know to which units those armed soldiers belonged and where they came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Colleagues from the HDZ in those days told me that these were members of their Territorial Defence. I know of one man, who was a local man, who came from the area of Croatia, from the Croatian army, Ivo, Suse. I also heard reports that there were people who came from Croatia, other people also, who had come from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were roadblocks set up on the road at that point, more or less March of 1992? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were not barricades. In fact, they were just people stopping vehicles, the people I have described. They were the ones who stopped those vehicles. I don't remember any particular barricades being put up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the accused Dario Kordic was involved in those incidents, stopping the vehicles that were coming out of the factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would meet Mr. Kordic in those days, and he did participate in those activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that same time, did you also participate in a television broadcast with Mr. Dario Kordic in Sarajevo, a broadcast in which the president of the parliament, Mr. Jozo Sekic, was also a participant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember a programme on the 21st of March. It was a Saturday. The programme was moderated by journalist Smiljko Sagolj. It was called "Vidokrug," or "Perspectives." I participated; the president of the assembly, Jozo Sekic; and Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the 21st of March; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The purpose of the broadcast, inter alia, was to mention the events that were taking place all around; that is, having to do with the weapons from that Bratstvo factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the programme had two aims. One was to show what was happening with the military industry, and especially the military industry in Novi Travnik, the Bratstvo factory. But I think another aim was to present for the first time the by then already formed Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show the Trial Chamber a short extract of that broadcast so that the witness can identify it. Let me state for the Trial Chamber that the witness appears on the videotape that's going to be shown, and perhaps a protective measure should also be ordered to preclude the witness's being recognised on that tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll have to show it in closed session; that's the only way that the witness can be protected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will be very short.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, you saw the short excerpt from the television programme that I referred to. Is that, in fact, the broadcast that took place in Sarajevo on the 21st of March, 1992, in which you yourself were a participant with the accused, Dario Kordic, and the president of the parliament, Mr. Jozo Sekic, everything under the control of the journalist Smiljko Sagolj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is that programme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, I'm now going to show you the transcript of the entire broadcast, which has several pages and which records some of the statements that you made and those of the journalists and the other participants. I would ask you to review the transcript which is referenced Z53.1 in B/C/S and Z53A in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The document should itself be protected insofar as it includes the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be possible, Witness P, to look at the last page of the document in which you appear. You say something right before the answer given by the accused. Could you give us a comment of what you meant in that statement and read out to us what the accused, Dario Kordic, answered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My comment was the following: I simply said what I knew and what my people felt, as well as a large number of citizens in those days, and that was that the Croatian community could not be established, as imagined, by the representatives of the political party of HDZ, and the comment of Dario Kordic was that no one has the right to stand in the way of the Croatian people in organising themselves as they wanted. That was the comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You could put the document down. Sometime after that television programme in March 1992, did you have the opportunity to see Dario Kordic again, who at that time was accompanied by soldiers in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came across Dario Kordic many times in that period, including in my own office where he would come, as well as in the vicinity of the Bratstvo factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to speak to us about the day that Dario Kordic came to your office to talk with you about the removal of two multiple-rocket launchers. Could you speak to us about that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dario Kordic came one day, one evening, together with soldiers that were escorting him; and Mr. Marinko Marelja, who was an owner of cafe Novi Travnik; and the president of the assembly, Jozo Sekic. As far as I remember, they were with him. He wanted to take with him some equipment. I remember they were two rocket launchers, VBRs as they were called. I know that there was a piece of paper. It was an ordinary piece of paper, torn off from a notebook, a cheque notebook, on which he wrote down that he would pay or return those pieces of equipment by the end of June. I don't know what happened in the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the document that you're speaking about one that Dario Kordic wrote himself and gave to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that document. I don't know where it ended up. I remember it very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a document. It is a document which was already admitted by another Trial Chamber. It is Z78.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The document is referenced Z78A, which is -- there's another 78B. I'm talking about 78A that I want you to show to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is Z78. It was admitted in April of last year. I think it is the handwritten document. Yes, it's that one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have ... that document. Yes, that is the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document with the signature of Dario Kordic is the one that you saw at the time, which was given to you by the accused; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand the document correctly, it is stated that the rocket launchers in question should either be paid for or given back on the 20th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is what it says here in the document and that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you remember, who was supposed to pay for those multiple-rocket launchers? Which authority was supposed to pay for them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic, as far as I can recollect, said that the defence secretariat of Busovaca would pay for it, because our joint Defence Ministry was still functioning in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the Minister was Jerko Doko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The accused, Dario Kordic, at that time was the office [sic] of that defence office for Busovaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that you have looked at another document that was given to you in advance. Could you look at it? It's a typed document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I see that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that document on the day that it was given to you or the other one was given to you, rather?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is one that I didn't see on that day. I only saw the first document, handwritten on a piece of paper with squares on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, was this document issued by the Bratstvo factory? Does it show the ordinary characteristics of that factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my view, that is not a document. The customary document issued by the factory would have a memorandum with the name of the factory, the telephone numbers and the faxes, and it would have to be stamped at the bottom saying who delivered what. I don't see that in this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that you've already said that the multiple-rocket launchers that are in question were never brought back to the Bratstvo factory, nor were ever paid for. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do I not know that they were paid for or returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea where those weapons went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Judging by what we heard, they went off towards Herzegovina or Croatia. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from the facts that we're speaking about that go back to approximately the 20th of April, 1992, as far as you know, did the accused, Dario Kordic, ever take other weapons from the Bratstvo factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that Kordic came to Novi Travnik municipality on several occasions and also to the Bratstvo factory. I saw him several times coming in an armoured vehicle up to the municipality where he held meetings. This was an armoured bus. He also went to the village of Margetici, which is in the immediate vicinity of the Bratstvo factory. Then he would come in a combat armoured vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Dario Kordic would come to Novi Travnik and go to the Bratstvo factory to take weapons, as you've just said, was he dressed in a uniform or was he wearing civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I mostly saw Mr. Kordic, at the beginning in the war, in military uniform. If my office -- he would come to my office wearing a military uniform and also on other occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he always accompanied by armed men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he came to my office, he was escorted by men in camouflage military uniform, under arms. Also, with him, Ignac Kostroman would come quite often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true, Witness P, that around June of 1992, before the conflict broke out on the 19th of June, that you and -- yourself and other Muslim authorities of the municipality received instructions from the HVO, according to which you were to submit or, rather, you would subordinate yourself to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that document personally in the Grand cafe. It was Ilija Zuljevic who had the document, and at the time he performed the function of Minister for Veterans Affairs in the republican government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I heard from colleagues in the HDZ of Novi Travnik that such demands had been made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told at the time that the request for your submission came from Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I'm sure it came from Mate Boban, but I do not recollect whose signature appeared on that document, but I know it was from the political and military leadership of Herceg-Bosna. In those days, the two were melded together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're speaking about the heading of the document that was given to you by Mr. Zuljevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that document, only he showed it to me and he said that that was something that we had to do, that we had to subordinate ourselves and place ourselves under the command of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you answer when he spoke to you about what the consequences of that kind of submission would be, if such submission would take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I asked him whether he knew what that document meant and what consequences it could have, and I told him that it could only have the consequence of bloodshed in Novi Travnik. He responded that it was an order that had to be carried out into practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Minister Zuljevic that you're speaking about, was he himself a member of the Croatian party, the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly he was a member of the HDZ. That is my conclusion, as he was a Minister on behalf of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, a little bit later, around the middle of May, 1992, after the HVO had taken over power in Busovaca, were you sent to Busovaca yourself at the request of Mr. Efendic and Mr. Jahic, who told you that you should speak with Dario Kordic and find out what happened in Busovaca? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went to Busovaca, and on that day your vehicle was stopped at an HVO checkpoint near Kaonik, around the Mediapan factory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is exactly what happened. I went in a red Golf vehicle with a driver and the vehicle was stopped at the checkpoint. It was a barricade really, at the place named Kaonik, at the bridge across the Lasva River, near the Mediapan factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, you didn't have an appointment with the accused, Dario Kordic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I did not have a scheduled appointment with Dario Kordic, but I hoped that he would receive us once we explained why we came to Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On two occasions you spoke to one or two other people; is that correct? Did you speak together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only had a driver with me, the person who drove me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to that checkpoint that was near the Mediapan factory, could you tell us in a few words what happened during the check and how the soldiers received you and then contacted the Tisovac centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were stopped in a very rude way. When I showed my personal ID and I asked to be received by Mr. Kordic, I heard a voice coming through the radio. They said, "Send the Turk over here," and they swore my mother, and "so we can cut his throat." Then the soldier said that Dario Kordic would guarantee that if I passed through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to hear those words clearly, because you were very close to the person who was holding the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very, very clear. I was outside, and I was standing next to the soldiers, and I heard this being said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you were authorised to go to the Tisovac Hotel, which at that point -- where Dario Kordic was, and that hotel is outside of Busovaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was allowed to come to the Hotel Tisovac, and after I waited for a period of time, Dario Kordic appeared with Ignac Kostroman. They were both wearing military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both of them were wearing uniforms; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were both wearing uniforms, and there was some kind of a headquarters there. I remember that there were a lot of soldiers there. I know that there was some bulldozer or some earth mover, so there was some earth being moved around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the meeting that you had with the accused Dario Kordic and Ignac Kostroman, did they explain to you that what was going on in Busovaca had happened because of an order which had been issued, according to which the Muslims had to subordinate themselves to the HVO, the Croats in Busovaca, and that the order had to be implemented, and that in addition there were a few extremist Muslims who wanted to prejudice the Croats in Busovaca? In any case, that's how they explained the take-over of power by the Croats in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what the explanation was of the political and military situation in the town of Busovaca. All Bosniaks were then expelled from the government, and all the institutions of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina were purged of all Bosniaks by the civilian government and the military government and all the institutions which were joined at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dario Kordic and Mr. Kostroman make any other comments about possible coexistence of the Muslims and Croats in the municipal institutions of the Herceg-Bosna Community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was really in dispute at the time. They insisted on the establishment of the Herceg-Bosna government, and later things would be as they would turn out to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they expressly tell you, on the day that you met with them, they could no longer accept a joint authority with the Muslims in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They insisted that the HZ-HB be implemented with all its institutions, and nobody paid any attention to what was going to happen to the Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a discussion with the accused Kostroman [sic] which lasted for about an hour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, somewhere around there. I believe that it may have lasted for about an hour. I know that they were busy, that they had other duties, they had other meetings; that is what they said. And so we stayed there for about one hour and then we parted. After my visit to Tisovac, on that same day, I visited a man called Husein Hadzimejlic, who at the time was in a position of the TO staff. I went to his home in Busovaca and told him everything that happened, that the Bosniaks were practically removed from all institutions of power, and he was scared and confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I'd like to correct something, if you allow me to, Mr. President. Let me point out, the question that I asked, reference is made to "the accused Kostroman"; I think I was referring to the accused Dario Kordic and Kostroman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, still in May 1992, on the 28th of May, 1992, specifically, was a new team put into place in the municipality of Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw this document at the centre for information and alert. That was the centre under my -- which was in my competence, under my authority, and I saw that this document was signed by Dario Kordic. I remember that Zvonimir Grahovac was there; he was the president. The vice-president -- I cannot recall exactly who the vice-president was. I know that Zlatan Civcija was head of the MUP, and the Department of Information and Propaganda was Marinko Marelja, the owner of the Grand Cafe. I was in a position to see all the names, I think about nine persons altogether, and no Bosniak was among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little bit later, on the 19th of June, 1992, Witness P, did you have meetings during the day with political and military representatives on the Muslim side, among whom were Mr. Saban Imamovic, and during the meetings, did you meet with the representatives of the Croatian side, that is, Mr. Jozo Sekic, Mr. Marinko Marelja, and could you speak to us briefly about what took place during those two meetings on the 19th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the morning we held a meeting with the president of the HDZ. At the same time, he was the president of the presidency of the Novi Travnik municipality, so this body had been established by the laws of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We met with him as both the president of the HDZ and the municipal assembly, so the political top, Croatian top of Novi Travnik who were there. But we were unable to reach any agreements as a result of this meeting. I attempted to call the next meeting with Zvonimir Grahovac, and he agreed to another meeting around 5.30 in the afternoon. Meanwhile, between these two meetings, I received information from Refik Lendo, the TO commander at the time, that we had received an ultimatum, and I heard it then directly from Marinko Marelja that if we did not militarily subordinate ourselves to the HVO, that we would be militarily defeated and that the HVO authority in Novi Travnik would be established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those meetings at the Workers' Centre in the city of Novi Travnik, the headquarters of the TO was attacked; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what happened. About 20 minutes into the meeting, we could hear shooting in town, and that was the attack on the TO headquarters, which was next to the police headquarters in Novi Travnik, practically next door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you were also able to hear that there were loudspeakers set up in the city being used by the HVO over which the HVO said that orders from the Muslim authorities had been given to surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what happened. The TO units were then called to subordinate themselves to the HVO. The HVO could do so because they had taken over the centre for information, and he was -- the head of the centre was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, check with the military command in Zenica, that's with General Merdan, that the order had never been issued, and, in fact, that it was false information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I checked that with General Merdan, who at that time was the commander of the regional staff of the Territorial Defence, and he told me that he was asking for an urgent cessation of hostility without any preconditions, and this is what I then transmitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then refuse to transmit the order to the Territorial Defence to surrender, and later on during that evening, while you were still at the Workers' Centre, you saw the chief of police arriving, Mr. Zlatan Civcija, who was accompanied by the person whose name was Ivo Skocibusic, who was known as Suse, and who was the chief of the HOS in Novi Travnik, and they were themselves escorted by a group of HVO soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what happened. Zlatan Civcija, as chief of police in Novi Travnik, came, and with him was Ivo Skocibusic, also known as Suse, and I heard them asking to see me in person. None of the Croatian negotiators came to our aid, to protect us, and they came and arrested us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they hit you at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at the time, I was also hit. I was kicked and hit with hands by soldiers who were there, and they were led by this Suse. And also a knife was placed under my throat, and they said, "This is now the Ustasha authority. You have no more life, and we will do the same to you as Chetniks are doing to Visegrad." And they also said, "We will kill you with bullets, we will hang you, and this will all happen to you now." And I said, "This only happens once."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were assaulted in that way, did you speak with the HOS chief and some of the soldiers at the Cafe Grand, whose owner was Marinko Marelja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know where the chief of police, Civcija, disappeared, but Suse and a group of policemen pushed me into a car. I don't know what make of a car, but I know that there were five or six of them, and they took me to the Grand Cafe, and while we were driving, they made threats to me. Then, when we came to the Grand Cafe, this Suse brought me out of the car and pushed me into the Grand Cafe. He hit me and said, "Get in, you pig." And he hit me here [indicates], and I still suffer from the consequences of this hit above the eye. I know that there were a number of the Croatian government there. Marinko Marelja, Civcija, Anto Zlatic, who was there without portfolio, as it were. So there were a number of people from the HVO government, and I think I mentioned four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that while you were at the Grand Cafe, one of the soldiers put his pistol into your mouth and joked around with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When they brought me to the Grand Cafe, I did not know what was going on. I know that one of the soldiers who had a camouflage uniform -- he was called Drazan; he was from Duvno or Tomislavgrad -- he put a pistol to me and cursed me, and he said, "Where are all the TO units? Where is Refik Lendo, the commander?" I know that Civcija and Marelja said that I had insisted on the legality of the BH government, and they cynically said, "Why doesn't President Izetbegovic help you now, and the presidents of the BH?" I stayed there for a while, in these circumstances, and then Marinko Marelja took me to a room which was on the premises of this cafe. It was a storage room. I spent the night there, until 9.00 next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you locked up in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I could not leave that room. I was locked in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that during that same night of the 19th of June, 1992, another representative of the Muslim delegation in Novi Travnik, Mr. Ragib Zukic, was also assaulted by members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I thought that this person actually had expired that night from the force of the blows that he received. He spent the night on the floor, but I saw him several days later. He was all black and blue. When he was on the floor, he was gurgling, and I thought that this was the -- the gurgling that comes at the time when somebody is dying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day we're speaking about, that is, the 19th of June, the individual whose name was Ivo Skocibusic, the head of the HOS, was wearing a black uniform and the others were wearing camouflage uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. I know that Skocibusic was wearing a black uniform all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you released the next morning, Witness P, and then taken to the Kasapovici sector, that is, the regional HVO commander, Mr. Filip Filipovic, who was the one who took you there; is that correct, to Kasapovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a man by the name of Filip Filipovic took me there, and I don't know what post he held at the time. He first took me to my parents', and then he took me to the village of Kasapovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, if you're moving on now to a different topic, that might be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now for a quarter of an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, I would like us to go back to the conflict of June 1992. Is it true that during that conflict, about ten soldiers from Busovaca were captured by the TO defence forces near the firemen's station in Novi Travnik and you were able to see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct. I personally saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the circumstances of your meeting with those soldiers was and where it took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met them in the afternoon in the village of Trenica, after a joint effort on the part of Croats and the Bosniak Muslims to calm down the passions. I came to talk to them and they then told me that they had been sent from Busovaca to the Novi Travnik area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself speak with those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I personally talked to them, and they also said that they were sent by Dario Kordic to Novi Travnik, and this is why they were there. They were all scared. Then they were released. They were kept in some kind of general store or maybe it was some kind of a cultural centre in that village, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness P, on several occasions you spoke about an individual whose name is Marinko Marelja, and you said that he was the owner of the Grand cafe where you were held for a night, and that he had responsibilities in the municipality where he was in charge of propaganda and information within the new municipality which had been set up in May, that is, the 19th of May, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct. He was in charge of information and propaganda, and he was a deputy, elected in the elections of 1990. Until then he was the president of a commission for appointments in the municipality at the local level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he an active member of the HDZ party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. From what I know, he was an active member of the HDZ party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, I'm going to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can tell the Trial Chamber that this document was previously admitted already. It is Z223.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, Witness P, after you've looked at the first page, this is a document which is dated 22 September, 1992, which was drafted in Busovaca at the Central Bosnia headquarters, and which deals with excerpts from the meetings of various Croat representatives in Central Bosnia. On the first page is a list of those people who participated in the meeting. Do you see the page I'm speaking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, under the section dealing with the municipality of Novi Travnik, who those individuals were who represented the city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see Marinko Marelja, vice-president of the Novi Travnik HVO. So this was some kind of a new appointment following the one in May of 1992. The president of the HVO was Jozo Sekic and Marinko was his deputy, and this is how he is titled here. There was also Jozo Sekic, who was the president of the HVO of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version of the document that you have, the name "Jozo Sekic" appears. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see him there. He's listed as the president of the HVO Novi Travnik, and Marinko Marelja vice-president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The name was left out on the English document. So my question is: The person that you spoke to us about, Marinko Marelja, was that the same person who appears as the representative of the Novi Travnik municipality on the document that you are looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is the only person by that name, Marinko Marelja, in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you review the second page of the document, Witness P? The first paragraph of page 2 deals with the municipality of Novi Travnik. Could you read the passage quickly and make a few comments to us about the report that was made about the events or the situation in the municipality of Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "It is estimated that the HVO hold about 70 per cent authority while the Muslims hold about 30 per cent. The question of special purposes production has to be urgently resolved. After an earlier confrontation with the Muslims the situation is tense but fairly peaceful. Recently the Croats have moved into about 400 apartments which were abandoned by Serbs without any coercion by the Croats but out of fear of Muslims." Now let me comment on this first section, if I may, right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, before we do that, what is the relevance of this? We have heard evidence about Novi Travnik, quite extensive evidence about the conflict there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was hoping that the witness, who had certain responsibilities in that municipality, could give us his opinion, but if you consider that it's not necessary, we can just move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's go on to the events that you deal with on pages 6 and 7 of the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, in July 1992 you were a participant -- well, leave aside the other document. We're going to speak about other things. In July 1992, you participated in other meetings with the HDZ and HVO representatives in Novi Travnik, who again said to you that they wanted the Muslims in the municipality to be subordinate to the Herceg-Bosna authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct. We refused this and requested to see what type of a model of a joint life we would be offered, but we asked that a platform of organisation be presented to us. This was the HZ-HB's own proposal, and we wanted to see what they had to offer but we never did. We didn't receive anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a document dated 7th of July, 1992. Please look at it and tell us whether the document relates to the events that you are speaking about. That is Z165-1, 165-1. That is a new document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You signed an agreement with Mr. Jozo Sekic, who had asked you to make proposals about how the HVO conceived of this joint authority.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not an agreement. This was a public notification and that a platform would be proffered, prepared in accordance with the concept of the HZ-HB, and that is what I have already stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never reached an agreement with the HDZ-HVO authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We received this prepared platform which contained the model of the administrative structure in accordance with the HZ-HB concepts. Of course, we turned it down. We wanted something that was not forced upon us by the other ethnic group. We were looking for a compromise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say, in passing, that this document, which has the witness's name, should also be covered by protective measures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving forward a little bit, in August of 1992 you were able to participate in celebrations, in a rally, that was organised by the Croats and which took place in front of the municipal building, where you saw many soldiers who had come to take an oath in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The accused Dario Kordic was present during the rally. You saw him in a camouflage uniform and he made a speech; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct. I saw him, and met him, and we exchanged greetings, and later on we sat at the hotel in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that during the speech the accused mentioned both the restructuring of the HVO and also stated that Novi Travnik would soon be Croatian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. Reference was made to the development of the HVO and to the fact that Novi Travnik would soon be taken by the Croats and that it would be a Croatian town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether on that day the accused Dario Kordic was escorted by a specific group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how he came to Novi Travnik, Dario Kordic, but I know that at this ceremony, when Croatian soldiers were taking an oath in front of the municipality building in Novi Travnik, but I know that a unit was present, like a honorary escort, which I was told was a unit of Jokers from Busovaca, that they were Dario's unit. I know that those young men reminded me of the young men I saw in Trenica, in the fire station, who were arrested there. They were all rather short and wearing military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the rally in Novi Travnik in August, there was also Marinko Marelja, whom we spoke about previously; Tihomir Blaskic; and the individual whose name was Ivo Skocibusic, the man who had hit you a little while earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. And that man wanted to say hello to me. I refused, because I wanted at least an apology from him for what he had done to me previously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Ivo Skocibusic, also known as Suse, did he also make a speech after Dario Kordic on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact order, but I know that Dario Kordic and Suse held speeches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to show you a document, Witness P, simply in order to try and situate the date that you're speaking to us about. This is a new document, reference Z191-1. Witness P, the document is dated 18th of August, 1992. It comes from Colonel Blaskic, and it deals with ceremonies of swearing in. In paragraph 2, under (b), it says that the ceremony would take place in Novi Travnik on the 23rd of August, 1992. Is the date the one which corresponds with the facts that you're speaking to us about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that was the date that corresponds to the event I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the ceremony, Witness P, is it true that the soldiers who had participated spread out in the city and started to shoot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what they did. The soldiers were shooting from different kinds of weapons in town, and the smell of gunpowder could be felt throughout the town, gunpowder and smoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In October 1992, that is, the 19th of October, 1992 to be exact, you were not in Novi Travnik when the second conflict broke out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was Friday, the 16th of October, when I went to Split from Zagreb, and I was away on that trip until -- the 18th was Sunday, 19th Monday. At half past 3.00, I left Split towards Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to be able to leave the city of Novi Travnik and to travel to Croatia, you had to receive a special permit from the HVO, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly. It was not possible to leave without that pass, and I had to get that pass from Marinko Marelja. I received it after a great deal of persuasion. And that applied to all Bosniaks; I think it was much easier for Croats. We all had to have those passes in order to able to move about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came back to Novi Travnik after your trip, you mentioned to those people who were there in the conflict about what had happened. Did people speak to you during those conversations about the role the accused Dario Kordic allegedly played during that second conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Excuse me, I object, Your Honour. That would be maybe hearsay -- bad word-- unreliable, because we don't know the source of the people, the context, and their basis for making these claims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lopez-Terres, if you would like to lay the foundation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, did you see a document, specifically a video document, in which the accused appeared during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that on the 18th, I was in Zagreb, and on the 24th, on the Saturday, I reached Novi Travnik. I saw what had happened, but I also received a videocassette on which I saw Dario Kordic at the hotel in Novi Travnik requesting the immediate arrest of Refik Lendo, for him to be tried, and he was the commander in Novi Travnik at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the conflict in October, did you notice that the Muslims in the city had been killed, that property belonging to Muslims had been destroyed by soldiers of the Novi Travnik municipality, but also by soldiers who came from outside that municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. After entering the town, I passed through the town and was able to see burnt and destroyed property, houses, businesses, apartments, of Bosniaks, Muslims. Among others, I saw some of my relatives' houses; they had been killed. And everything looked like something that consisted of ashes alone. All the houses had been burnt down -- that is, those under Croatian control. And I heard from many people who were there at the time that there were units present from all parts of Central Bosnia, Croatian units. From my relative's business premises, everything was taken away on a truck, and it was taken to Busovaca, and he was killed on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, I'm going to show you a document dated 5 November, 1992. This is a new document, and it's reference Z268-A, and 268 for the version in B/C/S. Witness P, the document is another one which comes from Colonel Blaskic. In the first part -- that is, the first paragraph of the document -- there is an order which is given to the HVO authorities in Novi Travnik that measures be taken so that houses belonging to well-known individual Muslims no longer be set on fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is certainly a good one, if only it had been issued before the conflict in October. But to be issued after that is rather ironic, after everything that could be destroyed had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, as far as you know, were the perpetrators of the murders that you spoke about, or the robberies and destruction, were they punished by the HVO authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware that any one of them was arrested, punished, or convicted for what he had done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, in December 1992, you participated in further negotiations with the HVO representatives. The negotiations had as their objectives to calm down the tensions within the municipality and possibly to set up a unified military command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. These were fresh efforts on our part to try and do something that would be satisfactory for both peoples, to set up some kind of an authority that would be accountable to both, to set up civilian structures and proper organisation of authority. That is what we could do as far as our possibilities allowed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there several meetings whose purpose was to set up this organ that you've just spoken about, and during the meetings, is it true that once again, the individual named Marinko Marelja was the representative of the Croatian authorities, the one who was the most active?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Upon entering the municipality building, or the office where I used to sit, there was a man called Marinko Marelja who said, "I am now the representative of the authorities. What can I do for you?" There were three of us. We sat down, talked to him. I don't remember whether there was anyone with him. Usually he would be alone, and negotiate by himself, because that was his nature. I know that Mr. Slobodan Praljak came in that period. I also know that Tihomir Blaskic would be with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness P, do you know where General Slobodan Praljak came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to what I know, Slobodan Praljak had come from Croatia, and he was in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the areas of Travnik, Turbe, the lines against the Serb aggressor at the time, so he was touring those lines and carrying out other tasks that he had. I know that I came across him there in Marinko Marelja's office, both him and Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This General Praljak, was he a general who came from the Croatian army? Do we agree about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Croatia. I later saw him on Croatian television, and I think that he was Brigadier General Slobodan Praljak. I know he wore a beard. He was tall and well built.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You again spoke about Marinko Marelja. Do you know whether this Mr. Marinko Marelja had any kind of friendly connections with the accused Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very frequently I sat with them in his cafe called Grand. Sometimes -- we would always sit together in the municipality building of Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them together on several occasions in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, I saw them together often. We would have coffee together, all three of us. I would be with them and with other people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that this Mr. Marinko Marelja participated in the funding of Anto Valenta's book on the partition of Bosnia and the transfer of populations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Marinko Marelja told me personally that he participated in the financing of the book and in the drafting of the book. In fact, it says in the book that he was one of the persons who financed it. I also heard in town that he was one of the people who organised the departure of Serbs from Novi Travnik via Busovaca and Kiseljak, two areas under Serb control. That is what I heard. I don't have any personal experience about it, but I heard a story that a very large convoy of people were stopped at the crossroads in front of Novi Travnik at the Travnik/Sarajevo road --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we can do without the stories. We will try and concentrate on evidence. Mr. Lopez-Terres, we must finish at 5.00. We ought to get through the witness's evidence in chief before then, so perhaps we could move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the first months of 1993, life was very difficult for Muslims in Novi Travnik, Witness P. There were two distinct areas in the city, one under the control of the HVO and an area where the Muslims lived, and at the time it was said that the Muslims were beaten, they were thrown out of their homes, and that there were also rapes of Muslim women; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was a period of divisions and checkpoints in town. And throughout Central Bosnia, Croats mostly controlled their areas whereas the Bosniaks kept to their own areas. I know that it was impossible for the Muslims, this whole period from the New Year until March or April 1993. It was unbearable for the Muslims. There was mistreatment, evictions, persecution, killings, also in that period. I know by name certain people who were killed in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period that we're speaking about, the crimes that you have mentioned involved various units. There was the local brigade, which was the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, and there was another one that came from the outside, made up of soldiers who were members of the Bruno Busic Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In town at the time, there were very many people from Herzegovina. They were known, the Hercegovci, who came with their equipment, soldiers in uniform, who belonged, as far as I know, to a brigade called Bruno Busic. Then in Novi Travnik there was the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, and as far as I can recollect, the commander of the HVO in those days was Mr. Mario Cerkez. I think I came across him at least twice at meetings held in that period in an attempt to prevent certain things from happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see that the soldiers who had come from Herzegovina had as their main responsibility terrorising the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our entire people felt this, that these were people who had come from there and who were terrorising them. And anyway, this was accepted by both the political and military leaders of Novi Travnik. For instance, when the Herzegovinians were supposed to go to a meeting held on the 13th of January, 1993, I know that President Jozo Sekic said that the Herzegovinians could not leave Novi Travnik because they hadn't finished the job they had come to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A final question, Witness P: During the conversations and meetings that you had with the representatives of the HVO of your municipality, whether it was Mr. Cerkez or Mr. Marelja, did they tell you whether they were obliged to speak with the accused Dario Kordic during the negotiations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that certain gentlemen said very frequently that they didn't dare do anything without their commander in Central Bosnia. In those days it was Dario Kordic who held the key role in the area of Central Bosnia. And very frequently the responsibility would be shifted onto him, that they couldn't do anything or were not allowed to do anything. That is what they said. Whether that was so, I don't know. That was the general impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have finished with the direct examination, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness P, you said then " ... that certain gentlemen said very frequently that they didn't dare do anything without their commander in Central Bosnia."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm just going to make a note. You then went on to say: "In those days it was Dario Kordic who held the key role ... and very frequently the responsibility would be shifted on to him, that they couldn't do anything or were not allowed to do anything. That is what they said."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those were the answers I was given very often.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: When you say "certain gentlemen" gave you those answers, can you tell us who it was or what type of people or category of people were saying this to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By way of an example, the president of the municipality of the HDZ, Jozo Sekic; or somebody who was a member of the HVO authorities, Anto Zlatunic; or Zoran Matosevic, who was secretary for defence at the time .... me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn now. Would you be back, please, Witness P, tomorrow at half past 9.00 to conclude your evidence. Would you remember not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over and, of course, don't let anyone speak to you about it. That includes members of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 4.57 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 22nd day of September, 1999 at 9.30 a.m.
